newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs end 3.7 pct higher, blue chips soar.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs end 3.7 pct higher, blue chips soar.

text.p: Brazilian shares surged 3.7 percent at the close in hefty trade, boosted by heavy buying of blue chips as domestic funds continue to flood the market with fresh cash, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 48 most traded stocks rose 466 points to close at 13,053 points in a day with a record number of trades, according to the Sao Paulo bourse's statistics.
The bolsa said there were 20,990 trades, totalling 1.31 billion reais ($1.2 billion).
Analysts said they are surprised at the bolsa, which on Wednesday reached its highest level so far this year, but most of them are unsure when the market will take a breather.
"We are little bit scared about the rally, but we have no idea when the market will take a break," a senior trader said.
Bellwether Telebras continued to post sharp gains today, soaring 4.78 percent to 168.70 reais.
Telebras voting stock jumped 3.9 percent to 152 reais.
The second biggest gainer among blue chips was federal power holding company Eletrobras, which rose 3.6 percent to close at 691 reais.
Eletrobras was followed by state oil firm Petrobras, which ended 2.9 percent higher at 319 reais.
Other power stocks also surged at the close on a positive outlook for the sector, higher corporate earnings forecasts, and bright privatization prospects, traders said.

Minas Gerais state electrical utility Cemig jumped 4.59 percent to close at 57 reais, while Sao Paulo power utility Companhia Paulista de Forca e Luz (CPFL) climbed 4.05 percent to close at 180 reais.
Despite those rises, a 1.01 percent decline in Eletropaulo shares restrained the rise in the Sao Paulo bourse's power sector index to just a slight 0.9 percent at 3,510 points.
The index comprises the nine most liquid stocks of the electrical sector.
